newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: NAVAN SAYS CHELOPECH MINE CLOSE TO TARGET IN H1.
newsitem.headline: NAVAN SAYS CHELOPECH MINE CLOSE TO TARGET IN H1.

text.p: Irish exploration group Navan Resources Plc said on Wednesday that the Chelopech gold-copper mine in Bulgaria performed close to target in the first half.

"At current metal prices, and even given the low volume of pyrite sales, we expect a profit and positive cashflow from operations in 1996 but whether the contribution will completely offset group overhead is less certain," Navan said in its half-year results statement.

The mine milled 259,905 tonnes compared with 197,736 tonnes in the corresponding period of 1995, grading 1.09 percent copper against 1.24 percent a year earlier and 3.36g/t gold compared with 3.78g/t to produce 26,078 ounces of gold and 4.93 million pounds of copper in concentrates sold.

During the first half, renovation to the principal shaft hoisting facilities was completed to enable an upsizing of capacity by 50 percent to approximately 750,000 tonnes per annum. In the mill, recoveries for both copper and gold steadily improved during the six months, Navan said.
The Chelopech operation achieved 96.3 percent of its planned metal recoveries to concentrates with the shortfall arising at period end due to the planned upgrading of the main shaft hoist.
This activity continued into July and production in the second half will not be able to recoup the shortfall, it said.
Navan said its Hungarian markets continued to be difficult with the government pursuing a high interest rate regime to curtail inflation.
Glass sand sales shrugged off difficulties and will increase profits for a fifth successive year while gypsum operations are showing signs of repaying the capital investment, Navan said.

Hungarian profits after tax were 333,000 after higher depreciation arising from the switch to the temporal accounting method. Cashflow was strongly positive due to the capital expenditure programme nearing its end.
"While the outlook for the second half is similar to the first, we are confident that there is a potential marked increase in profits awaiting the resumption of economic growth," Navan said.
In Spain, the board approved the expenditure of some 9 million for the development of the access ramp to the Aguas Tenidas orebody.

This ramp will enable detailed underground evaluation of the orebody for final mine design and also will provide primary access. Work is expected to begin in November with the award of the development contract.
Exploration activities on the groups' licences in the Pyrite Belt commenced with copper and gold as the primary targets whilst evaluation of the Los Santos tungsten project continued, Navan said.Z
